newsitem.title: UK: West Ham may consider stock market float this year.
newsitem.headline: West Ham may consider stock market float this year.

text.p: English premier league soccer club West Ham United could be considering a stock market flotation later this year, with a value of around 55 million stg, market sources said on Wednesday.
Sources believe West Ham had been waiting to secure its position in the premiership before making any decision on a listing.

The club has been camped near the relegation zone in recent weeks and in spite of finishing the season with a two-nil loss at champions Manchester United, West Ham wound up a safe fourteenth place in the league table, guaranteeing it another season in the potentially lucrative top flight.
Directors of the famous east London club declined to comment on the prospect of a flotation this year.

Spurred on by the stock market success of Manchester United -- whose shares almost quadrupled from the beginning 1996 to an all-time high of 737p on January 24 this year -- a spate of clubs have joined the market in recent weeks including Newcastle United and Aston Villa -- which finished second and fifth in the premiership respectively.
By 1430 GMT, Manchester United shares were trading at 595-1/2p, up 17-1/2p on the day, having fallen almost continuously since the club retained the premier league title on May 6.
